newsitem.title: GERMANY: German defence minister backs Bosnia operation.
newsitem.headline: German defence minister backs Bosnia operation.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe on Thursday defended the operation in which Bosnian Serb police chief Simo Drljaca was killed as peacekeepers tried to arrest him on war crimes charges.
Ruehe told reporters in Bonn the operation had conformed to the mandate laid down for the NATO-led stabilisation force (SFOR). "There was no violation of the mandate," he said.
Ruehe said no German soldiers were involved in the operation. He said it was not generally the task of the force to hunt down war criminals but this operation had been legitimate.

Drljaca, who headed the police in the northwestern town of Prijedor until last autumn, was shot dead after opening fire on the soldiers trying to arrest him, a NATO statement said. A British soldier was slightly wounded.
Prijedor hospital director Milan Kovacevic was arrested in a parallel operation and was to be turned over to the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague for trial.

Although their names were not on the official list of suspects published by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague, they had been mentioned in sealed indictments, according to a Western official in Sarajevo.
